newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap-Diesel slips on soft undertone.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap-Diesel slips on soft undertone.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps slipped late Tuesday as levels buckled under a soft physical market despite crude gains, brokers said.
They said deals were done at $22.25, $22.27 for July, with August traded at $22.80 and $22.85 and September at $22.40.
July swaps were last quoted at $22.20/$22.35 against $22.30/$22.40 seen earlier this morning.
Brokers said the soft undertone in the cash market has weighed on levels.
Traders said buyers were kept at bay, anticipating further price falls. Sellers said the lack of fresh buying interest, especially from China, has place pressure on prices.
Brokers said the regrade or the jet and gas oil spreads were hovering around $1.50-$1.60 for August with a lull seen in the jet swaps market.
Fuel oil swaps however maintained its strength late Asian trading day, supported by firm physical demand, traders said.
July fuel oil swaps narrowed from its morning quotes at $99.50/$100.50 per tonne, up by more than $1.00 per tonne from Monday.
They said a handful of local traders have emerged in the past two weeks soaking up any surplus supplies to cover their short-positions.
They said the buying support is likely to persist for the rest of the week.
Naphtha swaps rose in line with firmer crude prices. July naphtha was indicated at $20.45/$20.60 against Monday's $20.35/$20.55. August was quoted at $20.60/$20.75, up 10-15 cents.
